configurePresets.name: conf-screentest-waveshare-touch169-riscv-debug
configurePresets.description: Same board and same sources as conf-screentest-waveshare-touch169-debug, built for the RP2350's Hazard3 RISC-V cores instead of its Cortex-M33 pair. LIGHT_ARCH picks between the two archs the rp2350 chip entry registers, and light_resolve_pico_platform() turns that into PICO_PLATFORM=rp2350-riscv, from which pico-sdk selects its own RISC-V toolchain file. PICO_TOOLCHAIN_PATH is required rather than a convenience: the ARM trees find arm-none-eabi-gcc on PATH (PICO_TOOLCHAIN_PATH is empty in their caches) and there is only one PATH, so without it the SDK would search that same PATH for a riscv32-* compiler and find none. Setting it only here also keeps it out of the ARM trees. PICO_COMMON_LANG_FLAGS is pinned to pico-sdk's own second-choice entry to keep the Zcb/Zcmp code-size extensions (worth about 0.8%) -- see the vendor note for why its probe rejects them and what pinning costs.

PICO_COMMON_LANG_FLAGS: Setting this SKIPS pico_choose_compiler_flags()'s probe entirely -- it only probes when the variable is unset -- and pins the flags. The string is verbatim pico-sdk's own SECOND-choice entry from PICO_COMMON_LANG_FLAGS_LIST in cmake/preload/toolchains/pico_riscv_gcc.cmake.

What it buys, MEASURED on light_ui_touch169 Debug: 489 UF2 blocks down to 485, about 2KB or 0.8%. Modest on purpose -- the third entry the probe would otherwise settle on is rv32imaC, which already has standard compression, so the delta is only the extra Zcb operations and Zcmp push/pop. Do not confuse this with the ~17% by which the RISC-V image exceeds the ARM one; that gap is across two ISAs and two GCC versions and is not something these flags address.

Why the probe rejects it, which is NOT a Zcmp support gap: the probe's test file riscv_zcmp_test.c lists s0 as an asm clobber, and GCC 15 refuses s0 because it is the frame pointer at the -O0 the probe compiles at. That same file compiles clean at -O1, and cm.mvsa01/cm.mva01s assemble fine, so this toolchain (riscv-toolchain-15-x64-win, GCC 15.2.0) does support Zcmp.

Two costs of pinning. The assembler check the probe exists to perform no longer runs. And if pico-sdk revises its preferred flags, this string silently keeps the old ones -- re-check it against pico_riscv_gcc.cmake after an SDK bump.
Note that -mcpu=hazard3-rp2350, the list's FIRST entry, genuinely is unsupported by this GCC and is deliberately not what is pinned here.
CMAKE_<LANG>_FLAGS_INIT only applies on a first configure, so changing this needs a fresh build tree, not a reconfigure.
